column3: “he had married” renders “he had taken” (twice); NASB puts the second clause in parentheses.
NASB puts this verse in parentheses.
“If there is a prophet among you, I, the LORD” rearranges a difficult phrase, “if your prophet is, the LORD”; the meaning is uncertain.
“leprous” renders “struck with tsara’at” (twice), and NASB supplies “white” in “as white as snow.”
“do not account this sin to us” renders “do not lay sin upon us.”
“If … had but spit” renders an emphatic doubled verb, and “bear her shame” renders “be put to shame.”
